title: Tenant SteadyFlow Controller with Surge Credit Pooling
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated pools need predictable steady-state throughput guarantees, while still allowing occasional short surges without manual config. Current admission system enforces strict per-tenant qps caps and simple priority lanes which either waste headroom or allow noisy tenants to degrade other customers. Proposal: implement a SteadyFlow Controller — an admission shim that composes a per-tenant steady-rate allocator (soft guarantees) with a shared surge-credit pool and elastic soft-queueing. Key components: 1) SteadyToken allocator: each tenant has a long-window token bucket sized from their committed throughput (reserved units) that enforces steady guarantees but refills slowly to preserve long-term fairness. 2) SurgeCredit pool: a cluster-scoped ephemeral credit pool funded from unallocated capacity and autoscaler-provided burst tokens. Tenants can consume surge credits to temporarily exceed steady tokens for short intervals. 3) Elastic soft-queue: instead of hard rejecting excess requests immediately, we place burst requests into per-tenant soft queues with dynamic TTL and priority decay; queue length and wait-time budgets are negotiated with SLOs. 4) Overload shedding policy: when cluster headroom < threshold, apply graceful degradation via: a) suspend surge-credit issuance, b) probabilistic shed of best-effort requests, c) backpressure signals to client SDKs (HTTP 429 with retry-after and debug headers). 5) Autoscaler integration: the controller emits headroom signals and burst demand estimates to the Dedicated autoscaler so it can provision temporary capacity or revoke preemptible instances. Expected outcomes: consistent long-term throughput for committed tenants, better utilization by allowing safe short bursts, improved tail latency by preferring queueing over head-drop where appropriate. Implementation phases: design + sim, prototype in admission-proxy, staging tests with workload generator, gradual rollout behind feature flag, and finally GA with telemetry dashboards and SLO alerts.
comments: 2026-01-29 - Ayesha: Initial problem statement and proposal drafted. Added high-level component sketch and integration points with autoscaler and console.
2026-02-05 - Riley: Reviewed and suggested replacing per-request hard caps with token-bucket + soft-queue to reduce client retries; added queue TTL tuning parameters.

2026-02-12 - Marcus Lee (SRE): Asked for clear invariants around memory used by per-tenant queues; recommended bounded queue length and eviction policy. Added requirement to surface queue metrics to Console.
2026-02-18 - Riley: Added surge-credit accounting design: credits expire after 30s, can be topped up by autoscaler hints. Defined credit fairness window (rolling 5m).
2026-02-25 - Design review: agreed on 3-tier shedding modes (soft-defer, probabilistic-shed, hard-drop). PM requested customer-facing docs and SDK guidance for 429+retry-after handling.

2026-03-02 - Implementation: prototype admission-shim implemented in proxy; basic token-bucket and queue buffer added. Running synthetic bursts in local cluster. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/621

2026-03-09 - Observability: added Prometheus metrics: tenant_steady_tokens, tenant_surge_credits, tenant_soft_queue_depth, cluster_headroom_estimate. Dashboards draft: https://console.redwood-internal/dashboards/tenant-steadyflow

2026-03-12 - Staging run: 10k tenant-sim with 5% bursty traffic. Results: steady tokens preserved, queue p99 latency increased by 40ms for burst traffic, dropped requests reduced vs baseline. Found memory leak in queue ack path; tracking in ENG-514450.
acceptance_criteria: SteadyToken allocator enforces steady throughput for committed tenants over a 5m window with <1% violations under synthetic test.
SurgeCredit pool allows short bursts; surge credits are exhausted and honored correctly with expiry semantics.
Soft-queueing reduces hard drops by >=50% in burst scenarios without causing unbounded memory growth.
Headroom signals emitted and consumed by autoscaler hooks in staging run.
Telemetry surfaces tenant-level metrics and alerting rules for p99 queue latency and dropped-request rate.
